fact: The Interior Ministry announced a pilot of MOIEG-PASS, a selfie-biometric app built with the Communications and IT Ministry in which users scan their national ID and face to authenticate for a selected number of government services, with scaling to be decided after the pilot; as_of is the document's published date, none being given for the event.

Biometric Update reports Egypt is rolling out mandatory facial verification for SIM registration, in which an automated system compares the applicant's selfie with the photograph associated with the national ID before the operator may issue the SIM.
Biometric Update reports the NTRA began piloting, last year, a biometric eKYC system connected to Egypt's civil registry information, for identity verification at mobile operator branches.

Biometric Update reports Digified, licensed by the FRA, provides eKYC for lending, investment and insurance companies, including government data authentication by validating client information via national ID and mobile registry databases.

Egypt's Public Prosecution announced on 10 September 2026 that access to its electronic portal's personal-status document copy services is limited to users whose identity is verified through the Digital Egypt portal's digital identity.

Egypt's Public Prosecution announced on 1 September 2026 an electronic enquiry service on family cases and judgments, entry restricted to users whose identity is verified through the Digital Egypt portal's digital identity.

The Ministry of Social Solidarity launched on 29 August 2026 phase one of its digital foster-family services system, which the ICT ministry says is linked to the digital identity system so citizens can sign in securely.

NTRA's Araqamy ('My Lines') service, in the My NTRA app, lets users review mobile lines and e-wallets linked to their national identity cards; the document reports it in use, with an NTRA official speaking on 2026-08-17.

The Ministry of Communications and IT, with the Ministry of Interior, launched a biometric electronic verification and e-signature system for licensed telecom companies' apps, in a trial operating period.

The NTRA, with ITIDA, CyShield and licensed e-signature companies, launched a biometric verification and electronic signature system for remote telecoms services, running in a pilot phase that licensed mobile operators will make available gradually in their apps.
The regulator is adding face-recognition verification to the My NTRA app so only the data subject sees lines registered against their national number.

The Ministry of Interior's civil-registry kiosks, at 16 locations in 2024, have users enter their national-ID number and confirm identity by fingerprint or facial recognition before issuing documents.

fact: The Public Prosecution says its criminal-judgment enquiry service is provided through the enquirer's digital identity system, with the Ministry of Communications and IT, to verify the identity of the person asking.
Egypt's Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade says investors must hold a valid electronic signature token during company incorporation on the GAFI portal.

Masr Times reports that the communications ministry, through NTRA, launched the 'Digital Identity' biometric verification system, which matches a face and biometric data to Civil Status Authority records and is being applied on a pilot, gradual basis.
Masr Times reports the verification infrastructure is open to the four licensed mobile operators and integrates licensed e-signature firms, with services varying by operator during the pilot.

Egypt's FRA says its rules (Decision 186 of 2024, amended by Decision 133 of 2026) require regulated non-bank finance firms to query the validity of customers' national-ID data and mobile-phone ownership.
